title: Checking Consistency of the Manhattan Heuristic on a 4-Connected Grid
description: Collect free grid cells, yield unit-cost 4-connected edges from out_edges(cell), and run check_consistency on the Manhattan distance heuristic.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Unpack `H, W = grid.shape` and define `out_edges(cell)` to yield `(nbr, 1.0)` for every 4-connected neighbor returned by `grid_neighbors(grid, cell)`.

Collect all non-obstacle cells `free_cells` where `grid[y, x] == 0`, subsample `sample`, and call `check_consistency(sample, out_edges, h=lambda c: manhattan(c, goal))` to print `consistent` and `len(violations)`.

Look at how `out_edges(cell)` pairs with `manhattan(c, goal)` on line 12. Moving one step horizontally or vertically changes `manhattan(c, goal)` by `+1` or `-1`. This never exceeds the step cost `1.0` (`h(u) <= 1.0 + h(v)`).

steps.question: For a 4-connected grid with unit step cost `1.0` and `h(c) = manhattan(c, goal)`, what values will `consistent` and `len(violations)` have on lines 13-14?
steps.answer: `consistent` is `True` and `len(violations)` is `0`, because the Manhattan distance changes by at most `1` across any single 4-connected move.

steps.description: After scanning all `(y, x)` positions in the `18 x 28` grid to build `free_cells`, line 10 constructs `sample`.
Inside `check_consistency`, `out_edges(cell)` yields `(nbr, 1.0)` for each free 4-connected neighbor so `h(u) <= c(u, v) + h(v)` can be verified.
